title: Adaptive staffing lattice with tiered price triggers (Q2 2026)
content:
Executive summary:
This worksheet frames a flexible headcount lattice coupled to explicit pricing triggers across three commitment tiers (soft-commit, reserve tranche, burst). Purpose: give GTM + product concrete rules to reduce unit cost exposure while preserving SLA coverage for mid-surge workloads. Current draft focuses on Q2–Q4 2026 window and includes model-level assumptions for quantization and GPU-mix shifts.

Key takeaways (short):
- Target steady-state headcount for inference ops: 38 FTEs (engineers + SREs + capacity ops) with two seasonal cushions (3 FTE soft cushion, 6 FTE surge pool).
- Price trigger ladder: if 7-day rolling unit cost > baseline*1.12 => open soft-commit hiring hold; > baseline*1.25 => freeze discretionary hires + accelerate reserve tranche procurement; > baseline*1.45 => activate burst-conservation plan (feature throttles).
- Expected token-unit impact from quantization roadmap: -9% cost (conservative) to -18% (aggressive) by Dec 2026.

Assumptions (inputs used by tables below):
- Baseline token unit cost (hosted mix, blended) = $0.00095 per token (Feb 2026 observed).
- Monthly token demand scenarios: low=20B, base=45B, high=95B. Demand mix shifts assumed: q2 bias to chat (more tokens/req) -> average tokens/req +14%.
- GPU cost mix (weighted): A100-v3 (40%), L40 (30%), spot-sparse pools (30% effective price 0.6x on-peak).
- Headcount fixed cost per FTE fully-loaded = $14.5k/month (includes benefits, office, tools).
- Reserve tranche procurement (3-month commit) unit price discount estimated at 18% vs on-demand.
- Latency SLA breach cost proxy = incremental $0.12 per 1M tokens when SLOs degrade (used in opt-in decisions).

Scenario matrix (monthly view, simplified CSV):
scenario,monthly_tokens,Baseline_unit_cost,quant_savings,net_unit_cost,expected_monthly_cost,headcount_fte_required
low,20000000000,0.00095,0.09,0.0008645,17290000,28
base,45000000000,0.12,0.000836,37620000,38
high,95000000000,0.12,0.000836,79420000,52
Notes: quant_savings is conservative uplift from Optimize roadmap (applied multiplicatively). The expected_monthly_cost = monthly_tokens * net_unit_cost + headcount_fte_required * FTE_cost (FTE_cost = 14500).

Headcount phasing (quarterly snapshots):
- Q2 2026: Core 34 FTEs; soft cushion +3; contractors 5 (for onboarding bursts).
- Q3 2026 (base demand): ramp to 38 FTEs; hire plan: 4 infra, 1 finance/ops; maintain contractors 3.
- Q4 2026 (if high demand path materializes): accelerate to 52 FTEs + convert contractors; activate reserve tranche procurement and prioritize low-latency regions.

Price trigger rules (operational):
1) Monitor 7d rolling unit-cost by route/model via Console metric `unit_cost_7d`.
2) If unit_cost_7d > baseline * 1.12 for 3 consecutive days => freeze all non-essential hiring; pause non-critical experimental lower-tier tunnels. Notify: #finance-alerts, #eng-capacity.
3) If unit_cost_7d > baseline * 1.25 for 48h => accelerate procurement of 3-month reserve tranche for regional pools (pre-approved budget cap = $1.6M). Prepare PR for reserve spending.
4) If unit_cost_7d > baseline * 1.45 or capacity shortages cause latency SLO risk => issuer: Head of Platform + CFO convene emergency meeting; enable burst-conservation runbook (limit inference max tokens/req by 15% on lower-value customers, engage CS for high-tier exemptions).

Sensitivity steps (quick checklist for finance owner):
- Re-run matrix with GPU mix shift: move 10% weight from A100->spot-sparse and record net unit cost delta.
- Toggle quantization achievement to 0%/9%/18% in columns and capture threshold crossings for triggers.
- Stress test headcount hiring lead times: baseline hire lead = 8 weeks; slow hire lead = 16 weeks. Map to quarter of capacity attainment.

Sample recomputation formulas (for sheet implementers):
- net_unit_cost = baseline_unit_cost * (1 - quant_savings)
- expected_monthly_cost = monthly_tokens * net_unit_cost + headcount_fte_required * FTE_cost
- per-route_unit_cost = (model_compute_cost + region_markup + infra_amortization) / tokens_served_route
- trigger_ratio = unit_cost_7d / baseline_unit_cost

Action runbook (who does what):
- Finance (owner: Claire Zhang): Maintain monthly recalculation; publish a 1-page note to execs if any trigger crosses in two sequential weeks.
- Capacity Ops (owner: Benji Morales): Maintain reserve tranche vendor list; prepare vendor quotes and procurement timelines within 5 business days when threshold 1.25 hit.
- Platform Eng (owner: Diego Marquez): Prepare autoscale policy that can be toggled to conservative mode (batching up to 1.8x) and implement per-route throttles.
- CS/Pricing (owner: Aisha Khan): Pre-draft holdback communication for customers likely affected by burst-conservation (priority for enterprise with contracts).

Appendix A — Example walk-through: base -> high transition (timeline):
Week 0 (signal): 7d unit cost > 1.12 baseline for 3 days -> hiring freeze announced; weekend triage with capacity ops to check headroom.
Week 1: If cost continues -> finance executes budget pre-approval for reserve tranche; platform enables conservative autoscale; CS notified.
Week 3–6: Reserve tranche order placed (3 month commit). New capacity begins to show up around week 10–12 depending on vendor.

Appendix B — Quick numbers used in slide pack (for PM/CEO):
- Baseline monthly hosted cost @ base demand: ~$37.6M (incl. current FTE mix).
- Breakeven to avoid hiring freeze (with optimistic quant) moved to ~+18% demand growth vs baseline.
- If quantization misses and we hit high demand, marginal burn could require an extra $6–8M/month for 3 months to keep SLOs.

Open questions / items to resolve:
- Confirm vendor SLA on reserve tranche lead times (Benji to collect, due 2026-04-15).
- Validate quant savings with Research (PR#88 testing flagged slightly higher mem-copy overhead on L40 variants).
- Decide policy on enterprise carve-outs for burst-conservation (legal + CS to advise).

Notes to readers: this file is intended as a working worksheet. Numbers are intentionally conservative; please tag suggestions inline. If you copy into a Confluence page, keep the scenario CSV and formulas as separate code blocks for reproducibility.

Change log (brief):
- 2026-03-12 created initial lattice and baseline assumptions (Claire)
- 2026-03-27 added trigger cadence and procurement caps (Benji)
- 2026-04-08 updated quantization assumptions after PR88 review (Claire)

End of sheet.
